annotation.title_clean: Opinion 28/2024 on certain data protection aspects related to the processing of personal data in the context of AI models
annotation.title_en: Opinion 28/2024 on certain data protection aspects related to the processing of personal data in the context of AI models
annotation.summary_en: EDPB Article 64(2) GDPR opinion, requested by the Irish authority, on personal data in AI models. It covers when a model is anonymous, legitimate interest as a legal basis in development and deployment, mitigating measures, and the effect of unlawful development-phase processing on later use. It addresses general AI, with no robotics content.
key_provisions_or_claims: AI models trained on personal data are not automatically anonymous; supervisory authorities assess anonymity case by case.
Anonymity requires insignificant likelihood of extraction or of obtaining personal data through queries.
Legitimate interest requires a three-step test: legitimate interest, necessity, and balancing.
Mitigating measures may tip the balancing test but must go beyond measures GDPR already requires.
Unlawful development-phase processing may affect later processing, depending on three scenarios, with supervisory authorities using corrective powers.
